subject: Environment fit + data sovereignty: next actions
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Olmstead <julia@olmsteadhealth.com>, Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@olmsteadhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Environment fit + data sovereignty: next actions

Hi Julia / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposal for next steps so we keep momentum.

What we heard (high level)
- Primary constraint: data residency and strict segregation between customer data and other tenants; must be demonstrable in audit.
- Preference: single-tenant isolation for inference workloads; open to Dedicated capacity if network + KMS controls meet their bar, but leaning toward Private (VPC) if we can support customer-managed keys and control-plane isolation.
- Timeline: evaluation/POC within 6–8 weeks; procurement in Q1 2027 if POC successful.

Open questions we need from Olmstead to size options accurately
1) Do you require customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK) for model input/output storage and logs?
2) Is there any inbound connectivity to on-prem systems required (eg, database connectors)? If yes, list protocols/IP ranges.
3) Will Olmstead accept a Private deployment with Redwood-managed control plane but VPC peering, or does compliance require a fully customer-hosted control plane (on-prem)?

Suggested next steps
- Olmstead: confirm answers to the three questions above (reply to this thread).
- Redwood: we attach a short deployment matrix (Redwood-Deployment-Matrix.xlsx) that maps Hosted / Dedicated / Private against controls (KMS, audit logs, egress, network flow). Please review and flag any missing rows.
- Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60-minute follow-up with Rishi to walk the matrix and clarify networking/KMS specifics (proposed week of Oct 25).

Attachments: Redwood-Deployment-Matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — aim is to keep the POC scoped and avoid surprises in procurement.

—
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Julia Olmstead <julia@olmsteadhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@olmsteadhealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Environment fit + data sovereignty: next actions

Priya — thanks for the recap and the matrix. Quick answers inline below, then a couple of asks from our compliance/legal team.

Answers to your 3 bullets
1) BYOK: yes, we require customer-managed KMS for all persisted model inputs/outputs and for long-term logs. Keys must be in our tenant within AWS KMS or an HSM we provide.
2) Inbound connectors: we will need to call out to an internal metadata service (HTTPS REST) and a patient lookup Oracle DB for enrichment. We can provide IP ranges; DB connection will be over a NATed egress path from the VPC.
3) Control plane: Compliance strongly prefers the control plane to be customer-managed or at least logically separated. If Redwood offers a Private deployment where the control plane is in Olmstead's VPC (or deployed on-prem), that's preferred. If not, we need explicit contractual commitments about telemetry and no-data-access guarantees.

Compliance asks
- We need a short checklist of the evidentiary artifacts Redwood can provide during POC: SOC2 sections, network flow diagrams, KMS integration guide, and sample audit logs with redactions.
- Any chance you can share a proposed POC scope (what success looks like) and an ops-runbook for cutover?

POC timing: the week of Nov 8 looks good for us for a technical deep-dive.

Thanks — I’ll loop in procurement separately for contracting questions.

Julia Olmstead
Head of Platform Security | Olmstead Health
julia@olmsteadhealth.com | +1 617-555-0987

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Olmstead <julia@olmsteadhealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Environment fit + data sovereignty: next actions

Thanks Julia — that helps a lot. A few technical clarifications from the infra side so we can prepare accurate docs and a POC checklist.

Short technical Qs (please reply inline if possible)
- KMS/HSM: When you say "keys must be in our tenant within AWS KMS or an HSM we provide", do you need Redwood to integrate with your KMS via cross-account key policies, or will you provision an HSM that we can talk to over a private network?
- Control plane residency: would Olmstead accept a deployment where inference nodes and data plane are in your VPC and all customer data remains there, while a lightweight Redwood control plane (no access to customer S3/EBS) lives in a separate management account? If not, do you require fully customer-hosted control plane (we can discuss an on-prem package)?
- Network flows: for the Oracle DB, will you allow outbound (egress) connections from the inference VMs to your DB endpoint, or do you require the inference VMs to initiate a tunnel into your network? Please specify if DB traffic must be over a private link or via NAT egress.
- Audit logs: what retention window do you need for per-request metadata (tokens, timestamps, caller id)? Typical Redwood defaults are 30 days; we can extend and ship archived logs to your S3.

We will prepare the artifacts Julia requested: SOC2 extract, a draft network diagram for a Private/VPC deployment, and a KMS integration guide. Also attaching a short internal checklist (Redwood-Private-Checklist.pdf) that maps checks to owners — we can sanitize this before sharing with legal.

Proposed tech-deep-dive slots (all PDT): Tue Nov 9 10:00–11:00, Wed Nov 10 13:00–14:00, Thu Nov 11 09:00–10:00. Let us know which works.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Infrastructure & Reliability | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

Agreed next steps

- Redwood infra (Rishi): prepare a draft network diagram and KMS integration playbook + sample audit logs. Deliverable by Oct 29.
- Redwood sales (Priya): draft POC success criteria / runbook (attached: Olmstead-PoC-MAP.docx) and share contracting pre-reqs for a Private deployment.
- Joint: schedule the tech deep-dive — Julia indicated week of Nov 8 is good. Rishi proposed Nov 9/10/11 slots; please confirm one.

Attachments: Olmstead-PoC-MAP.docx, Redwood-Private-Checklist.pdf

If we can get the KMS preference and confirm one deep-dive slot, we'll circulate an invite and the artifacts for legal review.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping this moving.
